PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-06-29
60M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling generally well and staying active with regular walking. He takes his blood pressure medication every morning and checks readings at home twice weekly. Appetite is good, though his diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. He works as a store manager, mostly on his feet. Patient denies depression. No shortness of breath. Over recent months family has noticed periods of elevated mood and reduced need for sleep alternating with low periods, which the patient is open to exploring. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 190 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.
Psych: cooperative, normal speech rate today, linear thought process.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, eGFR stable post-transplant, basic metabolic panel otherwise normal.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 122/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. History of chronic kidney disease stage 4, resolved after kidney transplant. Graft function stable; continue immunosuppression as directed by transplant team. Labs reviewed and acceptable.
3. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and continuing daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
4. Concern for bipolar disorder; referred to psychiatry. Provided referral and reviewed warning signs to seek earlier care.
5. Health maintenance: colorectal screening up to date; influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 6 months, sooner as needed.
